Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office files ordinary paperwork by indexing dated records in defined document classes, validating required fields against standard templates, and routing entries through designated intake channels for storage and retrieval.
2) What occurred: The actor created multiple duplicate copies of a single dated admission document, altering the ticket identifier field on each copy to appear unique. The actor listed the copies across several resale channels, assigning each listing a buyer-facing price. The actor transmitted the first copy's barcode data to an identified buyer via a direct message channel. The actor transmitted a fabricated confirmation email, bearing a dated record of entry clearance, to the identified buyer. The actor initiated a reverse-charge transaction request against the original account and disabled the account's notification field to suppress audit alerts.
3) Materials/access observed: One original admission document with a unique ticket identifier field; three duplicate admission documents with altered ticket identifier fields; two resale channel listings; one direct message channel transmission; one fabricated confirmation email with a dated entry record; one chargeback request form; one account settings panel.
4) Indicators & artifacts: Multiple admission documents sharing a single original issue timestamp but distinct ticket identifier fields; a chargeback request form referencing a ticket identifier field that does not match the original issue record; a confirmation email originating from an unregistered domain; a direct message channel containing barcode data transfer between two identified accounts; an account notification field set to disabled state concurrent with the chargeback request submission.
